issue_context.title: [feat] move updater bundle target to a separate field
issue_context.body:
### Describe the problem

About updater configs, I think updater is not really a "target" anymore

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would suggest we change our config files a bit, removing updater from bundle targets, instead making it a separate field, like:

`updater: true | false | "legacyZipped"`

- `true`: only generates/reuses non-zipped installers/updaters
- `legacyZipped`: keep the v1 behavior 

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_
comments: I think that makes sense but will need an equivalent `--updater` CLI flag.

review_comments: let's add a couple more tests for `targets: "updater"` and `targets: "all"`
@lucasfernog should we make `V1Compatible` the default and emit a warning that it will be changed in v3?

Enable generating updaters only makes sense if they use the updater plugin, I don't think enable should be the default (or maybe we detect plugin updater field), and `V1Compatible` should never be the default, I'm so worried about we will end up having everyone still using `V1Compatible`, and warning on default value is pretty weird as well

Maybe we change the name to `LegacyV1Compatible` so that people will know it's not supposed to be used (maybe some more details in the description), and should really only be there because of `tauri migrate`
The problem is in order for apps built with v1, to migrate to updater v2, they need to push zips so v1 can update v2, then they can stop using them
I already made `tauri migrate` to migrate the old updater to `V1Compatible`, I don't think there's any reason to make it the default, we can emit a warning though

that's what I am suggesting, keep the current default and constantly emit warnings that it will be removed in v3. This allows users to migrate their v1 apps to v2 and then later from v2 to v3 there won't be an issue.
kk, I can add that warning tomorrow
